$comment: Byte budgets for scripts/check-budgets.mjs (pnpm build), from the redesign's §5.2. JS = gzip -9 of the first-party <script src> files a modern browser runs (noModule left out). HTML = the prerendered page, raw and gzip -9, the inline RSC payload included.
Routes that exist today hold the §5.2 JS gates (all 13 are within them) and their measured HTML plus 5% (the ratchet, measured on 2026-09-28 from the 0.6.0 tree at e2efe48).

/docs/: D1 replaces the hub (§3.4: about 150 words and the cards), so it has the docs pages' HTML gate (90,000 B raw, 15,000 B gzip, as its JS budget already is the docs pages' 156,000) as its target, enforced from the moment src/content/docs/quick-start.mdx (D1's) exists. /checks/: §5.2 gives the hub no number of its own (it is neither a check page nor one of the 'other pages' the redesign leaves alone), so it kept the ratchet until E1 lowered it to what C1's hub measured on 2026-09-28 (147,722 B raw, 25,926 B gzip) plus 5%.

'/' also has the §5.2 homepage gate as its target (135,000 B raw, 25,000 B gzip): a note while the old homepage is built, and a budget that fails the build from the moment src/content/home.ts exists (target.enforceWhen, the same switch check-copy uses for the 750 words).

New docs pages (/docs/*/) and check pages (/checks/*/) hold the §5.2 gates from their first build. /_design/ is internal and holds only the chunk bans and the font budget. '*' is the default for any other page (the §5.2 JS gate for other pages, and 90,000 / 18,000 B of HTML): a new kind of page gets it unless it has its own entry.

lazy.gsapGzip is the after-load motion budget plus the on-approach one (32,000 + 22,000), over every lazy chunk with GSAP's core, ScrollTrigger or DrawSVG in it; lazy.maxChunkGzip the after-load budget, for any one lazy chunk. lazy.search is §5.2's 'search on open ≤ 16,000 (dialog + pagefind.js)': the lazy chunk that imports /pagefind/pagefind.js plus pagefind.js itself (12,951 B at gzip -9 in Pagefind 1.5.2, leaving the dialog about 3,000 B), a note until H1's src/components/search exists, then a budget; the lab's request log measures the same on a real open.
arbitraryValues: class strings like px-[72px] in src (tests left out), no growth over the 139 of today.

/checks/csrf/, /checks/paywall-trust/, /checks/verbose-errors/ and /checks/write-access/ carry the full exported spec of a real run, which Next.js also embeds in the page's inline RSC payload for hydration, so it is in the HTML twice; removing either copy would take the spec out of the server HTML (no-JS readers, search). They hold their measured HTML of 2026-09-28 plus 5% instead of the check pages' 15,000 B gzip (decision 2026-09-28-long-spec-check-page-budgets).
